grow/one: One unit after a three by three conv sees a three by three patch of the input. That patch is its receptive field: three wide.
grow/two: Stack a second three by three layer. Its unit sees three units below it, and together those see five input pixels. The layer added two.
grow/three: A third layer reaches seven. Each stride one layer adds F minus one, so L layers of three by three see one plus two L.
stride/jump: A stride speeds this up. After a stride two layer, neighboring units sit two input pixels apart.
stride/adds: So the next three by three layer spans twice as much: it adds two times two, four. Three becomes seven.
stride/deep: This is how a deep network's last layers come to see the whole image, while every filter stays small.
why/same: Two stacked three by three layers see five by five, exactly like a single five by five filter.
why/fewer: But they need fewer weights: nine plus nine, eighteen, against twenty five.
why/more: The saving grows with depth. Three layers of three by three see seven by seven with twenty seven weights; one seven by seven filter needs forty nine. Same view, fewer weights.
